transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time. It's probably just a small thing, but... I've been having a little trouble at work. I supervise a retail team, and I always try to be really clear and helpful for them, but lately... 

Well, when I try to explain things to them, like the inventory numbers or, you know, the weekend schedule... my words just start jumping around a bit. Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm on about Thursdays, and then... the church grill, or my boss's tone of voice. And my team, they just kind of look at me like they can't follow what I'm saying at all. 

It's a bit embarrassing, honestly, because I really want to do a good job for them. I hope I'm explaining this okay to you... does that make sense?
When your words jump around like that, does it feel like your thoughts are racing through your mind faster than usual?

Oh, um... no, I don't think they're racing. I hope it's okay to say that, I definitely don't want to give you the wrong impression or be difficult. 

It's not like a high-speed chase up there or anything like that. My thoughts actually feel like they're moving at a pretty normal speed, honestly. It's just that... well, the topic just sort of shifts without me noticing right away. It's like I'm walking at a regular, calm pace, but suddenly the scenery around me has changed, if that makes sense? 

I really do try my best to stay focused and keep everything organized for my team, I promise I do. Am I explaining that alright for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you heard any voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?

Oh, goodness, no. I haven't... I haven't heard anything like that at all. Just the usual everyday sounds, you know, the store radio and the customers talking. Nothing out of the ordinary. 

I really hope that's a good thing—I certainly wouldn't want to add to whatever is going on with me and make your job harder! But no, no voices or anything like that. Does that help narrow things down for you? I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can.
Have you felt like people are watching you, talking about you behind your back, or trying to harm you?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, retail can be a little gossipy sometimes, just people chatting in the breakroom, but... no, I definitely don't feel like anyone is out to get me or watching me or anything sinister like that. 

I really try to get along with everyone at the store, and I think they generally like me. I hope they do, anyway. I always try to be a supportive supervisor. So, no, I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I hope that's helpful for you to know. Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
About how long ago did you first start noticing this trouble with your words jumping around?

Well, I suppose... um, it's been about six months now? Give or take a little. I really hope I shouldn't have come in sooner, I just didn't want to make a fuss over nothing or waste your time, you know? 

But yes, it's been around six months since I first started noticing those... well, those sort of jumbled explanations when I'm helping out on the sales floor. And sometimes I just have these odd little stops where I pause for a moment while I'm talking to my team. It's really not too terrible, I promise, and I always try to smooth it over so the customers don't mind. 

Does that timeline make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture and being a good historian for you.
